catalog_quote: Todas as dicções acabadas nas quatro ultimas vogaes tem o accento na ultima, e notão-se com circumflexo. Algumas acabadas em e que parecem ter o accento na penúltima, é por serem compostas, ut icatúpe de icatú, e pè ... As acabadas em a partim na ultima, e notão-se com o mesmo accento, ut tatá, partim na penúltima, e notão-se com o acuto, ut óca. As monosyllabas com accento grave, ut pè, tè, rihò, rihu, etc. Os verbos pela maior parte tem o accento na ultima, em qualquer consoante ou vogal que se acabem, ut ajucâ, amondéb, etc. Os mais dos acabados em i, praecedente vocali, tem o accento na penúltima, ou se hão de chamar contractos, ut acái, aiucéi. ... sweep_summary: this search of works with stress in the title for Tupinambá (tupi1273, in catalog as 'morphological', deciding source Anchieta 1595) turned up a single title-keyword item, Mayer 1903 'Die Rhythmik des Hans Sachs' (PBB 28), which is a German-literature article on Hans Sachs's verse rhythm mis-attached to tupi1273 in Glottolog 5.1; it is irrelevant, unread and priority none. No new source was downloaded. The directory already held, from the 2026-09-16 check, the two authoritative modern descriptions (Rodrigues 1958 Phonologie der Tupinambá-Sprache; Ferraz Gerardi 2023 RRG grammar) plus Mistieri 2010; I re-read the stress sections of both main works and wrote there. Best statement read: Gerardi 2023 sec. 2.3 (p.58) — stress fixed on the last syllable, penult/antepenult only via unstressed suffixes, clitics and composition, contrast only in derived words — which, together with Rodrigues 1958 sec. 4.7.1 ('von einem morphologischen Standpunkt aus prädiktabel'), confirms the catalog's 'morphological' coding and should replace Anchieta 1595 / Navarro / Wikipedia as the deciding modern source. Neither Rodrigues nor Gerardi is yet in the per-language bibliography (BIB_BY_LANG has no 'Rodrigues'/'Gerardi' entry for tupi1273).

new_statements.quote: The stress is fixed, occurring on the last syllable (72), but it might fall on the penultimate (73) or antipenultimate (74) under specific morphophonological conditions. (72) a. [ka."ruk] 'urine' ... d. [ja.ka."re] 'caiman' ... the stress falls on the penultimate syllable of derived words, either through suffixation (a,b) or through cliticization (c) and composition (d,e). (73) a. /juka/ + /-saβa/ → [ju.ka."sa.βa] 'way of killing' ... c. /a-/ + /so/ + /=ne/ → [a."so.ne] 'I shall go' ... (74) a. /mono/ + /reme/ → [mo."ndo.re.me] ... Contrastive stress can only be seen in morphologically derived words (75). a. /aβ/ + /-a/ → ["a.βa] 'feather' b. /aβa/ → [a"βa] 'man'
new_statements.citation: Ferraz Gerardi, Fabrício. 2023. A Role and Reference Grammar Description of Tupinambá. Tübingen: Tübingen Library Publishing. 459 pp. (open access, hdl 10900/142263)
new_statements.locator: sec. 2.3 'Prosody', printed p.58 (pdf p.81); text-layer lines 2587-2616 of the held
new_statements.reading: Stress falls on the final syllable of the (bare) stem; penultimate or antepenultimate surface stress arises only when unstressed suffixes or enclitics (-a, -saβa, =ne, -reme, -ramo..) follow the stem, so placement is predictable from morphological structure and surface contrast exists only in derived words. Rodrigues 1958 sec. 4.7.1 (held, pdf p.129, printed p.121) says the same in German: 'alle auf Konsonant endenden Wörter den Akzent auf der letzten Silbe haben.. Wörter ohne Suffixe sind, wie jeder blosse Stamm, auf der letzten Silbe betont.. Aus dieser Situation ergibt sich, dass das Auftreten des Akzents von einem morphologischen Standpunkt aus prädiktabel ist.' Both confirm the catalog's 'morphological' coding.

new_statements.second_reader_bearing_note: No correction. set by morphology stands (stem-final stress; atonic suffixes/enclitics leave it in place, giving surface penult/antepenult only in derived words). Do not read Gerardi's opening line 'The stress is fixed, occurring on the last syllable' as a fixed and weight-blind final rule: his own (73)-(75) show surface non-final stress in derived words and a stem-vs-derived contrast ["a.βa] 'feather' (/aβ/+/-a/) vs [a"βa] 'man'. audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the Anchieta 1595 deciding quotation is verbatim at the stated locator in the scanned file we hold (l.1019-1080 = Platzmann p.10-11), and the Navarro and Jensen secondary quotes are verbatim at their stated lines. (2) The classification rested on a 1595 missionary grammar plus a pedagogical grammar and a comparative chapter, with the record itself carrying the caution 'needs a primary description before it is relied on'. sources.quote: Reviews Anchieta, Rodrigues 1958, Lemos Barbosa 1956 and Cardoso 1990 (lists of atonic suffixes/enclitics -a, -i, -pe, -ne, -mo, -bo, -(r)eme, -(r)amo ...), tests them against 366 rhyme-position words in Anchieta's Tupi poems (217 paroxytone, all ending in a listed atonic suffix; 146 oxytone), and concludes: 'podemos concluir que o tupi é uma língua de acento morfológico (o acento elucida a estrutura morfológica de uma palavra), em contraposição ao chamado acento rítmico'.
sources.note: Accent-specific study testing the atonic-suffix lists against rhyme positions in Anchieta's Tupi verse; concludes 'acento morfológico'. Low weight (BA monograph) but directly on point.
